contexts.text: Rivers of honey and butter () = things spiritual and celestial. AE 619:6.
To eat honey and butter () = the Celestial Spiritual. (Honey = what is from the Celestial. AC 5620:2.)
Its affections of truth and good are described by fine flour, honey, and oil ().
Honey () = what is happy thence.
Flowing with milk and honey (Illustrated.) ... Honey = the abundance of happinesses (from celestial spiritual things). AC 5620:9.
Their happy things are... honey ().
A little resin and a little honey () = the truths of exterior natural good, and its delight.
The reason honey = delight, is that it is sweet; and everything sweet in the natural world corresponds to what is delightful and pleasant in the Spiritual World.
That honey = delight. Illustrated.
Honey () = what is from them, thus, what is happy, pleasant, and delightful.
Honey () = the pleasantness of (the Spiritual). AC 9995:4. ( = external good. AC 10540:3.)
Honey () = the pleasantness and delight from the affections of knowing and learning goods and truths celestial and spiritual.
To suck honey out of the rock () = the delight from scientific truths.
To satisfy them with honey out of the rock () = the delight from the truths of faith. ( = the delight of good. AE 374:11.)
A Land of the olive of oil and of honey () = spiritual good and its pleasantness. ( = the Church as to the good of love, and its delight. AE 374:7.)
Sweeter than honey and the dropping of the honeycombs () = the delights from good and the pleasantnesses from truth.
His food was locusts and wild honey () = the Word, such as is its literal sense as to good; its delight is signified by wild honey. AC 7643:10. AC 9372:8.

The delight of truth Divine as to the external sense is described by honey in ; and ... That truth Divine in the external form appears delightful, is signified by the taste (of the Book) being sweet as honey. Explained.

(Thus) honey = the delight which is from good and truth, or from the affection of them; and, in special, it = external delight; thus that of the exterior Natural. As this delight is such that it is from the world through sensuous things, and thus contains within it many things from the love of the world, the employment of honey in the meat-offerings was forbidden... (); where honey = such external delight, which, as it contains something of the love of the world, was like leaven, and therefore was prohibited. AC 10137:12.
Things which derive anything from fatness, to the same extent = good; as milk, honey, gums.
The various goods of the Ancient Church... are signified by honey, oil, butter, milk, and fat ().
Flowing with milk and honey () = the derivative pleasantness and delight... Honey = delight. ( = where there are gladness and joy. AC 8056.)
Honey is predicated of the good of truth.
The taste of it was like that of a cake in honey () = good, that it is delightful, as is that which is made good from truth by means of delight... Honey = natural delight.
It is said wild honey, because by a field is signified the Church.
Honey = external delight, thus that of love in both senses.
To a Land flowing with milk and honey () = pleasantness and delight from the good of faith and of love... Honey = celestial good, which is the good of love.
Honey () = its external delight.

The butter and honey which He shall eat = the goods of love; butter, the good of celestial and spiritual love; honey, the good of natural love. By these words is meant that He would appropriate to Himself what is Divine even as to the Human. (Divine natural good is signified by honey. AE 617:8.)
To suck honey out of the rock = that they had natural good through truths. (Honey = good and natural delight. AE 375:36.) (Honey = natural good. AE 411:7.)
Honey () = the delight thereof.
Honey () = the good of love in the natural man.
Honey () = the Natural as to the good from which is truth.
Wild honey = what is sensuous as to good.
Honey () = natural good, or that of the external man. AE 619:11. ( = good from a natural origin. AE 1153:3.)
Butter and honey shall everyone eat who is left in the Land (); butter and honey = spiritual good and natural good. ( = the delight of spiritual and natural good. AE 619:5.)
It shall be in thy mouth sweet as honey () = exterior delight... Sweet as honey = the delight of natural good.
Honey = the delight of natural good. Illustrated.
Honey () = the delight of natural good; consequently... the Divine Natural; thus His Human... exterior.
As honey = the delight of natural good... the Land of Canaan... was called a Land flowing with... honey. Illustrated... These goods together with their delights are signified by milk and honey.
That there was much honey in Canaan at that time, on account of the Lord's Church being there, is evident from .

The reason Jonathan's eyes were opened by his tasting the honey, was that honey corresponds to natural good and its delight; and this good gives intelligence and enlightens... As also is read in Isaiah, that he should eat butter and honey in order to know how to refuse the evil and choose the good...
The same as is signified by butter and honey, is signified by oil and honey, in the following places. Illustrated.
Honey () = the delight of natural love.
Honey out of the rock () = the delight of natural good through truths from the Lord.

As there must be both (spiritual and natural good), therefore in (all these) passages, it is said butter and honey, milk and honey, fat and honey, and oil and honey; and by... honey is signified the good of natural love, together with their delights. Illustrated.
Oil and honey () = the good of love in the internal man and in the external man.

As the goods with which man is affected are delightful, it is said that they are sweeter than honey and the dropping of the honeycombs; and that the words of Jehovah are sweeter... than honey in the mouth. Sweet = delight; honey, natural good; and the dropping of the honeycombs, natural truth. And as honey = natural good, and the mouth = what is external, it is said, than honey in my mouth.

As honey = the good of the natural man, John's... meat was... wild honey... The wild honey = the good of the natural man, (which is the same thing as) the natural good such as is the Word in its ultimate sense...

The reason... no honey was to be employed in the offerings made by fire... was that... honey = the delight of the good of the natural man; and, in the opposite sense, the delight of his evil, which is also like leaven when it is mixed with such things as signify holy interior things; for natural delight derives what belongs to it from the delights of the loves of self and of the world; and as the Israelitish nation was in these delights more than other nations, they were forbidden to use honey in their sacrifices.
Samson... found in the lion's carcase a swarm of bees and honey (), by which was signified, that after that faith is dissipated, in its place there succeeds the good of charity.
It was in my mouth as sweet as honey () = that the Word as to the sense of the letter was as yet perceived as the delight of good...
